question: What threefold divine affirmation does the prologue of John's Gospel make regarding the Word in the beginning?
opt1: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God
opt2: In the beginning the Word was created, and the Word was an angel, and the Word brought light
opt3: In the beginning was the Spirit, and the Spirit moved upon the waters, and the Spirit was God
opt4: In the beginning was the light, and the light shone upon the darkness, and the darkness fled
correct: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God
explanation: John 1:1 establishes the eternal pre-existence, distinct personhood, and absolute deity of the Logos. John 1:1 (KJV) - "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God."

question: What comprehensive declaration does John make regarding the agency of the Word in the creation of all things?
opt1: By his wisdom the foundations of the heavens were established
opt2: All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made
opt3: He created the angels first, and through them he formed the earth
opt4: The earth and all that is therein were fashioned by the counsel of the prophets
correct: All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made
explanation: Scripture attributes total creative agency to the divine Word without exception. John 1:3 (KJV) - "All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made."

question: How did John describe the incarnation of the Word and the glory witnessed by the disciples?
opt1: And the Word appeared as an angel, and showed his power unto the kings of the earth
opt2: And the Word took the likeness of a prophet, and spake with the tongue of cherubim
opt3: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth
opt4: And the Word descended from heaven in a pillar of fire, and rested upon the temple mount
correct: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth
explanation: The incarnation represents God taking on genuine human nature while displaying divine glory. John 1:14 (KJV) - "And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth."

question: In contrasting the dispensations of redemptive history, what did John declare was given by Moses versus what came by Jesus Christ?
opt1: The law was given by Moses, and the prophets came by Jesus Christ
opt2: The covenants were given by Moses, and righteousness came by Jesus Christ
opt3: The temple was given by Moses, and eternal glory came by Jesus Christ
opt4: For the law was given by Moses, but grace and truth came by Jesus Christ
correct: For the law was given by Moses, but grace and truth came by Jesus Christ
explanation: Moses mediated the holy Law, but fullness of grace and truth arrived in Jesus Christ. John 1:17 (KJV) - "For the law was given by Moses, but grace and truth came by Jesus Christ."

question: When the priests and Levites from Jerusalem asked John the Baptist who he was, what did he confess using the words of Isaiah?
opt1: I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, Make straight the way of the Lord, as said the prophet Esaias
opt2: I am Elias, sent before the great and dreadful day of the Lord
opt3: I am the prophet that should come into the world to restore the tribes
opt4: I am the messenger of the covenant, who shall suddenly come to his temple
correct: I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, Make straight the way of the Lord, as said the prophet Esaias
explanation: John defined his prophetic identity through Isaiah 40:3 as the preparatory voice. John 1:23 (KJV) - "He said, I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, Make straight the way of the Lord, as said the prophet Esaias."

question: What supreme Messianic title did John the Baptist proclaim when he saw Jesus coming unto him the next day?
opt1: Behold the Lion of the tribe of Juda
opt2: Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world
opt3: Behold the King of Israel and the Lord of glory
opt4: Behold the Prince of Peace, born of the house of David
correct: Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world
explanation: John identified Jesus as the sacrificial Lamb ordained to bear away the world's sin. John 1:29 (KJV) - "The next day John seeth Jesus coming unto him, and saith, Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world."

question: What visible sign did John the Baptist bear record of seeing that confirmed Jesus as the One who baptizeth with the Holy Ghost?
opt1: The waters of Jordan turning to wine
opt2: A pillar of cloud resting upon his shoulder
opt3: I saw the Spirit descending from heaven like a dove, and it abode upon him
opt4: Seven torches of fire burning before his face
correct: I saw the Spirit descending from heaven like a dove, and it abode upon him
explanation: The visible descent and abiding of the Spirit marked the Messiah. John 1:32 (KJV) - "And John bare record, saying, I saw the Spirit descending from heaven like a dove, and it abode upon him."

question: What new name did Jesus give unto Simon the son of Jona when Andrew brought him to Jesus?
opt1: Boanerges
opt2: Barnabas
opt3: Didymus
opt4: Cephas, which is by interpretation, A stone
correct: Cephas, which is by interpretation, A stone
explanation: Jesus surnamed Simon as Cephas (Peter), meaning a stone. John 1:42 (KJV) - "And he brought him to Jesus. And when Jesus beheld him, he said, Thou art Simon the son of Jona: thou shalt be called Cephas, which is by interpretation, A stone."

question: Where did Jesus tell Nathanael he had seen him before Philip called him?
opt1: When thou wast under the fig tree, I saw thee
opt2: Standing by the sheep gate in Jerusalem
opt3: Praying on the housetop at Capernaum
opt4: Washing thy nets by the sea of Galilee
correct: When thou wast under the fig tree, I saw thee
explanation: Jesus revealed His omniscience by seeing Nathanael under the fig tree. John 1:48 (KJV) - "Nathanael saith unto him, Whence knowest thou me? Jesus answered and said unto him, Before that Philip called thee, when thou wast under the fig tree, I saw thee."

question: What greater celestial vision did Jesus promise that Nathanael and the disciples should see hereafter?
opt1: The sun darkened and the moon turned into blood
opt2: Hereafter ye shall see heaven open, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of man
opt3: Twelve thrones set for the judgment of the tribes of Israel
opt4: The new Jerusalem descending from God out of heaven
correct: Hereafter ye shall see heaven open, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of man
explanation: Jesus applied Jacob's ladder vision to Himself as the true bridge between heaven and earth. John 1:51 (KJV) - "And he saith unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Hereafter ye shall see heaven open, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of man."

question: In what city did Jesus attend a marriage with his mother and disciples on the third day?
opt1: Capernaum of Galilee
opt2: Bethlehem of Judaea
opt3: Cana of Galilee
opt4: Nazareth of Galilee
correct: Cana of Galilee
explanation: The wedding where Jesus performed His first miracle took place in Cana of Galilee. John 2:1 (KJV) - "And the third day there was a marriage in Cana of Galilee; and the mother of Jesus was there:"

question: How many waterpots of stone were set there after the manner of the purifying of the Jews, and what was their capacity?
opt1: Twelve waterpots, containing ten ephahs apiece
opt2: Seven waterpots, containing seven omers apiece
opt3: Four waterpots, containing forty baths apiece
opt4: Six waterpots of stone, containing two or three firkins apiece
correct: Six waterpots of stone, containing two or three firkins apiece
explanation: There were six stone waterpots used for ceremonial purification, holding two to three firkins each. John 2:6 (KJV) - "And there were set there six waterpots of stone, after the manner of the purifying of the Jews, containing two or three firkins apiece."

question: What observation did the governor of the feast make to the bridegroom after tasting the water that was made wine?
opt1: Every man at the beginning doth set forth good wine; and when men have well drunk, then that which is worse: but thou hast kept the good wine until now
opt2: This wine is mingled with sweet spices from the mountains of Lebanon
opt3: Why hast thou spared the vintage until the feast is well nigh ended?
opt4: Never was such vintage pressed from the vineyards of Engedi
correct: Every man at the beginning doth set forth good wine; and when men have well drunk, then that which is worse: but thou hast kept the good wine until now
explanation: The banquet master commended the superior quality of the miraculously provided wine. John 2:10 (KJV) - "And saith unto him, Every man at the beginning doth set forth good wine; and when men have well drunk, then that which is worse: but thou hast kept the good wine until now."

question: What was the significance of this first miracle in Cana of Galilee as recorded by John?
opt1: It silenced the Pharisees who sought to accuse him
opt2: This beginning of miracles did Jesus in Cana of Galilee, and manifested forth his glory; and his disciples believed on him
opt3: It fulfilled the prophecy of Hosea concerning the vintage of Israel
opt4: It prompted the Sanhedrin to investigate his lineage
correct: This beginning of miracles did Jesus in Cana of Galilee, and manifested forth his glory; and his disciples believed on him
explanation: Christ's first sign manifested His divine glory and deepened His disciples' faith. John 2:11 (KJV) - "This beginning of miracles did Jesus in Cana of Galilee, and manifested forth his glory; and his disciples believed on him."

question: What instrument did Jesus make when he drove out of the temple those that sold oxen, sheep, and doves, and poured out the changers' money?
opt1: A whip of braided leather
opt2: A rod of olive wood
opt3: A scourge of small cords
opt4: A staff of cedar
correct: A scourge of small cords
explanation: Jesus fashioned a scourge of small cords to cleanse His Father's temple. John 2:15 (KJV) - "And when he had made a scourge of small cords, he drove them all out of the temple, and the sheep, and the oxen; and poured out the changers' money, and overthrew the tables;"

question: What rebuke did Jesus give to them that sold doves in the temple courts?
opt1: Woe unto you that turn the sanctuary into a den of robbers
opt2: Take these offerings unto the high priest outside the gate
opt3: Why pollute ye the courts of the Lord with unwashen hands?
opt4: Take these things hence; make not my Father's house an house of merchandise
correct: Take these things hence; make not my Father's house an house of merchandise
explanation: Jesus defended the sanctity of His Father's house against commercial exploitation. John 2:16 (KJV) - "And said unto them that sold doves, Take these things hence; make not my Father's house an house of merchandise."

question: What scripture did the disciples remember after Jesus cleansed the temple?
opt1: The zeal of thine house hath eaten me up
opt2: Holiness becometh thine house, O Lord, for ever
opt3: Mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people
opt4: The Lord whom ye seek shall suddenly come to his temple
correct: The zeal of thine house hath eaten me up
explanation: They recalled Psalm 69:9 regarding passionate zeal for God's house. John 2:17 (KJV) - "And his disciples remembered that it was written, The zeal of thine house hath eaten me up."

question: How many years did the Jews state that Herod's temple had been in building when Jesus said, 'Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up'?
opt1: Seventy years
opt2: Forty and six years
opt3: Thirty and three years
opt4: Fifty and two years
correct: Forty and six years
explanation: The Jews noted that construction on the temple had spanned forty-six years. John 2:20 (KJV) - "Then said the Jews, Forty and six years was this temple in building, and wilt thou rear it up in three days?"

question: Of what temple was Jesus actually speaking when he declared, 'Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up'?
opt1: The heavenly tabernacle not made with hands
opt2: The spiritual assembly of the faithful
opt3: He spake of the temple of his body
opt4: The altar of burnt offering in Zion
correct: He spake of the temple of his body
explanation: John clarifies that Jesus was prophesying His own bodily resurrection on the third day. John 2:21 (KJV) - "But he spake of the temple of his body."

question: Why did Jesus not commit himself unto the many who believed in his name when they saw his miracles at the Passover feast in Jerusalem?
opt1: Because they were under the authority of the Roman governor
opt2: Because the Sanhedrin had posted guards around his lodging
opt3: Because his hour was not yet come to be glorified
opt4: Because he knew all men, And needed not that any should testify of man: for he knew what was in man
correct: Because he knew all men, And needed not that any should testify of man: for he knew what was in man
explanation: Jesus exercised divine insight into the fickle hearts of superficial believers. John 2:24-25 (KJV) - "But Jesus did not commit himself unto them, because he knew all men, And needed not that any should testify of man: for he knew what was in man."

question: Who was Nicodemus, who came to Jesus by night acknowledging him as a teacher come from God?
opt1: A man of the Pharisees, named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews
opt2: A Roman centurion stationed at Fort Antonia
opt3: A chief scribe of the lineage of Aaron
opt4: A wealthy publican from Jericho
correct: A man of the Pharisees, named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews
explanation: Nicodemus was both a Pharisee and a prominent member of the Jewish ruling council. John 3:1 (KJV) - "There was a man of the Pharisees, named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews:"

question: What essential spiritual requirement did Jesus state as necessary to see the kingdom of God?
opt1: Except a man offer sacrifices according to the law of Moses
opt2: Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God
opt3: Except a man give half his goods to the poor and fast weekly
opt4: Except a man be circumcised in the temple of Jerusalem
correct: Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God
explanation: The spiritual rebirth (regeneration) is the indispensable requirement to perceive God's kingdom. John 3:3 (KJV) - "Jesus answered and said unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God."

question: What two elements did Jesus identify as necessary for entering into the kingdom of God?
opt1: Water and blood
opt2: Fire and the holy law
opt3: Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God
opt4: Repentance and fasting
correct: Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God
explanation: Entrance into the kingdom requires spiritual cleansing and regeneration by the Holy Spirit. John 3:5 (KJV) - "Jesus answered, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God."

question: What natural element did Jesus use as an analogy to explain the mysterious, sovereign working of the Holy Spirit in regeneration?
opt1: The rain that falleth upon the mountains
opt2: The river that floweth into the sea
opt3: The seed that sleepeth in the earth
opt4: The wind bloweth where it listeth, and thou hearest the sound thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit
correct: The wind bloweth where it listeth, and thou hearest the sound thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit
explanation: The Spirit's sovereign, invisible operation is likened to the blowing of the wind. John 3:8 (KJV) - "The wind bloweth where it listeth, and thou hearest the sound thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit."

question: What Old Testament historical event did Jesus cite to prefigure his own crucifixion and the salvation of believers?
opt1: And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up
opt2: As Abraham offered up Isaac upon Mount Moriah
opt3: As Jonah was cast into the deep from the ship
opt4: As the brazen altar was set up in the court of the tabernacle
correct: And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up
explanation: The lifting up of the bronze serpent in Numbers 21 foreshadowed Christ being lifted up on the cross. John 3:14 (KJV) - "And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up:"

question: According to John 3:16, what motivated God to give his only begotten Son that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life?
opt1: His hatred of the serpent and judgment upon the nations
opt2: For God so loved the world
opt3: His desire to restore the Davidic kingdom on earth
opt4: The righteousness and prayers of the saints
correct: For God so loved the world
explanation: God's infinite love for the world is the supreme fountainhead of redemption. John 3:16 (KJV) - "For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life."

question: What is the condemnation of unregenerate men as articulated by Jesus?
opt1: That they refused the circumcision of their fathers
opt2: That they could not keep the ten commandments in perfection
opt3: That light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil
opt4: That they offered blemished sacrifices upon the altar
correct: That light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil
explanation: Condemnation is rooted in men actively preferring moral darkness over divine light. John 3:19 (KJV) - "And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil."

question: Where was John baptizing when the Jews questioned his disciples, and why did he choose that location?
opt1: In the pool of Siloam in Jerusalem, because it was near the temple
opt2: At the ford of Jabbok, because Jacob wrestled there with God
opt3: In the river Kishon, because Elijah slew the prophets of Baal there
opt4: In Aenon near to Salim, because there was much water there
correct: In Aenon near to Salim, because there was much water there
explanation: John baptized in Aenon near Salim due to its abundant water supply. John 3:23 (KJV) - "And John also was baptizing in Aenon near to Salim, because there was much water there: and they came, and were baptized."

question: What famous principle of humility did John the Baptist proclaim regarding his relationship to Christ?
opt1: He must increase, but I must decrease
opt2: I am the prophet, but he is the king
opt3: My baptism with water shall outlast his words
opt4: Let all men honor the herald as they honor the Lord
correct: He must increase, but I must decrease
explanation: John joyfully yielded preeminence to Christ with these immortal words. John 3:30 (KJV) - "He must increase, but I must decrease."

question: What eternal consequence awaits those who believe on the Son versus those who believe not the Son?
opt1: Believers shall obtain riches, but unbelievers shall wander in exile
opt2: He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life: and he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him
opt3: Believers shall escape earthly sickness, but unbelievers shall perish in the grave
opt4: All shall ultimately be restored when the temple is rebuilt
correct: He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life: and he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him
explanation: The ultimate divide in human destiny hinges upon faith in God's Son. John 3:36 (KJV) - "He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life: and he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him."

question: Near which historical parcel of ground did Jesus rest at Jacob's well in the Samaritan city of Sychar?
opt1: The cave of Machpelah which Abraham purchased from Ephron
opt2: The threshingfloor of Araunah the Jebusite
opt3: The parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph
opt4: The field of Ephraim near the wilderness
correct: The parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph
explanation: Sychar was situated near the historic plot Jacob bequeathed to Joseph. John 4:5 (KJV) - "Then cometh he to a city of Samaria, which is called Sychar, near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph."

question: At what hour of the day was Jesus sitting wearied on Jacob's well when the woman of Samaria came to draw water?
opt1: The third hour
opt2: The ninth hour
opt3: The twelfth hour
opt4: About the sixth hour
correct: About the sixth hour
explanation: Jesus rested at the well at approximately midday (the sixth hour). John 4:6 (KJV) - "Now Jacob's well was there. Jesus therefore, being wearied with his journey, sat thus on the well: and it was about the sixth hour."

question: What did Jesus describe as the property of the living water that he would give unto whoever drinks of it?
opt1: It shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life
opt2: It shall cleanse him from all leprosy and physical disease
opt3: It shall sweeten all bitter waters throughout the land of Samaria
opt4: It shall satisfy his bodily thirst for forty days and nights
correct: It shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life
explanation: The living water of the Holy Spirit becomes an internal, everlasting spring. John 4:14 (KJV) - "But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life."

question: What personal fact concerning the Samaritan woman's domestic life did Jesus disclose to her?
opt1: Thou hast hidden seven talents of silver under thy hearth
opt2: For thou hast had five husbands; and he whom thou now hast is not thy husband: in that saidst thou truly
opt3: Thou hast refused to care for thy aging parents in Samaria
opt4: Thy father was a priest of Baal upon Mount Gerizim
correct: For thou hast had five husbands; and he whom thou now hast is not thy husband: in that saidst thou truly
explanation: Jesus supernaturally revealed her marital past and current cohabitation. John 4:18 (KJV) - "For thou hast had five husbands; and he whom thou now hast is not thy husband: in that saidst thou truly."

question: What theological truth did Jesus declare regarding God's essential nature and the true worshippers the Father seeks?
opt1: God is a consuming fire, and only the circumcised may approach his throne
opt2: God is light, and only those who offer incense in Jerusalem please him
opt3: God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth
opt4: God is eternal, and sacrifices upon Mount Gerizim are accepted by him
correct: God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth
explanation: God's spiritual essence necessitates worship characterized by the Spirit and truth. John 4:24 (KJV) - "God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth."

question: What direct revelation did Jesus give when the woman said, 'I know that Messias cometh, which is called Christ'?
opt1: Go thy way and search the scriptures of Moses
opt2: Ask the priests in Jerusalem, for they keep the records
opt3: The Messiah shall appear upon Mount Zion in power
opt4: Jesus saith unto her, I that speak unto thee am he
correct: Jesus saith unto her, I that speak unto thee am he
explanation: Jesus unveiled His Messianic identity plainly to the Samaritan woman. John 4:26 (KJV) - "Jesus saith unto her, I that speak unto thee am he."

question: What did Jesus declare was his meat when his disciples prayed him to eat?
opt1: My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, and to finish his work
opt2: Man doth not live by bread only, but by every word of God
opt3: My meat is to offer prayers night and day for the lost sheep
opt4: I have eaten hidden manna which angels brought from heaven
correct: My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, and to finish his work
explanation: Christ's true nourishment was accomplishing His Father's redemptive mission. John 4:34 (KJV) - "Jesus saith unto them, My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, and to finish his work."

question: What vision of spiritual harvest did Jesus present to his disciples regarding the fields?
opt1: The harvest must tarry until the early and latter rain
opt2: Say not ye, There are yet four months, and then cometh harvest? behold, I say unto you, Lift up your eyes, and look on the fields; for they are white already to harvest
opt3: The labourers are many, but the fields are choked with tares
opt4: The sickle cannot be put to the grain until the seventh month
correct: Say not ye, There are yet four months, and then cometh harvest? behold, I say unto you, Lift up your eyes, and look on the fields; for they are white already to harvest
explanation: Jesus urged urgency, pointing out that souls were ripe for harvest immediately. John 4:35 (KJV) - "Say not ye, There are yet four months, and then cometh harvest? behold, I say unto you, Lift up your eyes, and look on the fields; for they are white already to harvest."

question: What did the Samaritans declare concerning Jesus after hearing him for two days in their city?
opt1: We know that this is a great prophet of Israel
opt2: He hath confirmed the righteousness of Mount Gerizim
opt3: This is indeed the Christ, the Saviour of the world
opt4: He is the teacher sent to reconcile Samaria and Judaea
correct: This is indeed the Christ, the Saviour of the world
explanation: The Samaritans recognized Jesus' universal saviorhood beyond ethnic borders. John 4:42 (KJV) - "And said unto the woman, Now we believe, not because of thy saying: for we have heard him ourselves, and know that this is indeed the Christ, the Saviour of the world."

question: At what hour did the fever leave the nobleman's son in Capernaum when Jesus said in Cana, 'Thy son liveth'?
opt1: At the third hour
opt2: At the sixth hour
opt3: At midnight
opt4: Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him
correct: Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him
explanation: The servants confirmed the fever vanished at the exact seventh hour Jesus spoke. John 4:52 (KJV) - "Then enquired he of them the hour when he began to amend. And they said unto him, Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him."

question: By what market in Jerusalem was the pool called in the Hebrew tongue Bethesda, having five porches?
opt1: By the sheep market
opt2: By the fish gate
opt3: By the horse gate
opt4: By the valley gate
correct: By the sheep market
explanation: Bethesda was located near the sheep market in Jerusalem. John 5:2 (KJV) - "Now there is at Jerusalem by the sheep market a pool, which is called in the Hebrew tongue Bethesda, having five porches."

question: For how many years had the infirm man at the pool of Bethesda suffered from his infirmity before Jesus healed him?
opt1: Twelve years
opt2: Thirty and eight years
opt3: Forty years
opt4: Eighteen years
correct: Thirty and eight years
explanation: The man had been paralyzed for thirty-eight long years. John 5:5 (KJV) - "And a certain man was there, which had an infirmity thirty and eight years."

question: What three commands did Jesus give to the infirm man at the pool of Bethesda?
opt1: Wash thy face, confess thy sins, and go to the priest
opt2: Offer two pigeons, stand upon thy feet, and rejoice
opt3: Rise, take up thy bed, and walk
opt4: Step into the pool, wash seven times, and depart
correct: Rise, take up thy bed, and walk
explanation: Jesus spoke the authoritative command of instantaneous healing. John 5:8 (KJV) - "Jesus saith unto him, Rise, take up thy bed, and walk."

question: What warning did Jesus give to the healed man when he found him afterward in the temple?
opt1: Speak not of this miracle unto the Roman guards
opt2: Return not to the pool of Bethesda on the sabbath
opt3: Pay thy vow unto the altar before sundown
opt4: Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee
correct: Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee
explanation: Jesus reminded him of the spiritual perils of returning to sin. John 5:14 (KJV) - "Afterward Jesus findeth him in the temple, and said unto him, Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee."

question: Why did the Jewish leaders seek the more to kill Jesus after he healed the man at Bethesda?
opt1: Because he not only had broken the sabbath, but said also that God was his Father, making himself equal with God
opt2: Because he entered the Holy of Holies without priestly garments
opt3: Because he forbade the people to pay the temple shekel
opt4: Because he consorted with the Samaritans and ate with tax collectors
correct: Because he not only had broken the sabbath, but said also that God was his Father, making himself equal with God
explanation: They sought His death for calling God His Father and claiming equality with God. John 5:18 (KJV) - "Therefore the Jews sought the more to kill him, because he not only had broken the sabbath, but said also that God was his Father, making himself equal with God."

question: What did Jesus say regarding the Father's commitment of judgment unto the Son?
opt1: The Father judgeth the Gentiles, but the angels judge Israel
opt2: For the Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son
opt3: Moses shall judge the living, and the Son shall judge the dead
opt4: Judgment is reserved solely for the archangel Michael
correct: For the Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son
explanation: The Father delegated universal judicial authority exclusively to the Son. John 5:22 (KJV) - "For the Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son:"

question: What solemn promise of immediate spiritual transition did Jesus declare for whoever hears his word and believes on Him that sent him?
opt1: He shall inherit earthly crowns in the kingdom of David

John 5:24 (KJV) - "Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation; but is passed from death unto life."

question: What two distinct resurrections did Jesus foretell when all that are in the graves shall hear his voice and come forth?
opt1: The resurrection of the priests and the resurrection of the people

explanation: Christ distinguished the resurrection of life from the resurrection of damnation. John 5:29 (KJV) - "And shall come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life; and they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of damnation."

question: What command and testimony concerning the Holy Scriptures did Jesus deliver to the Jewish leaders?

correct: Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me
explanation: The entire Old Testament scriptures point forward to and testify of Jesus Christ. John 5:39 (KJV) - "Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me."

question: Whom did Jesus say would accuse the unbelieving religious leaders to the Father, even the one in whom they trusted?
opt1: Abraham
opt2: Moses

explanation: Moses himself wrote of Christ, rendering their rejection of Jesus an indictment under the Law. For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me."

question: What question did Jesus ask Philip to prove him when seeing the great company coming unto him?

John 6:5-6 (KJV) - "When Jesus then lifted up his eyes, and saw a great company come unto him, he saith unto Philip, Whence shall we buy bread, that these may eat? And this he said to prove him: for he himself knew what he would do."

question: What provisions did Andrew, Simon Peter's brother, find with a lad among the multitude?

question: How many baskets were filled with the fragments of the five barley loaves which remained over and above unto them that had eaten?
opt1: Twelve baskets

correct: Twelve baskets
explanation: Twelve full baskets of leftovers were gathered after five thousand men ate. John 6:13 (KJV) - "Therefore they gathered them together, and filled twelve baskets with the fragments of the five barley loaves, which remained over and above unto them that had eaten."

question: What comforting words did Jesus speak to his terrified disciples as he walked toward their boat on the stormy sea of Galilee?
opt1: Peace, be still, and let your hearts be quiet

correct: It is I; be not afraid
explanation: Jesus calmed their fears with His reassuring divine presence. John 6:20 (KJV) - "But he saith unto them, It is I; be not afraid."

question: What exhortation did Jesus give to the multitude regarding the kind of meat they should labour for?
opt1: Seek the bread of angels which fell in the wilderness

correct: Labour not for the meat which perisheth, but for that meat which endureth unto everlasting life, which the Son of man shall give unto you
explanation: Jesus redirected their focus from physical food to eternal spiritual life. John 6:27 (KJV) - "Labour not for the meat which perisheth, but for that meat which endureth unto everlasting life, which the Son of man shall give unto you: for him hath God the Father sealed."

question: When the people asked, 'What shall we do, that we might work the works of God?', what was Jesus' answer?
opt1: Keep all the commandments and the ordinances of the temple
opt2: Offer sacrifices of praise and fast twice in the week
opt3: Give your bread to the hungry and clothe the naked
opt4: This is the work of God, that ye believe on him whom he hath sent
correct: This is the work of God, that ye believe on him whom he hath sent
explanation: The supreme work God requires is saving faith in His sent Son. John 6:29 (KJV) - "Jesus answered and said unto them, This is the work of God, that ye believe on him whom he hath sent."

question: What supreme 'I AM' declaration did Jesus make regarding true spiritual sustenance?
opt1: I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst
opt2: I am the living vine that bringeth forth fruit throughout all seasons
opt3: I am the hidden manna sent down from the highest heavens
opt4: I am the true shepherd that feedeth his flock in green pastures
correct: I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst
explanation: Jesus declared Himself to be the Bread of Life satisfying all spiritual hunger. John 6:35 (KJV) - "And Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst."

question: What promise of unconditional divine reception and eternal security did Jesus give to all who come to him?
opt1: He that cometh to me shall be tested by fire seven times
opt2: All that the Father giveth me shall come to me; and him that cometh to me I will in no wise cast out
opt3: Whosoever striveth shall enter if his righteousness endure
opt4: He that keepeth my commandments shall never be forsaken
correct: All that the Father giveth me shall come to me; and him that cometh to me I will in no wise cast out
explanation: The Father's sovereign drawing guarantees that no seeking sinner will ever be cast out. John 6:37 (KJV) - "All that the Father giveth me shall come to me; and him that cometh to me I will in no wise cast out."

question: What confession did Simon Peter make when Jesus asked the twelve, 'Will ye also go away?' after many disciples walked with him no more?
opt1: Lord, thou art our King, and we will fight for thy kingdom
opt2: Master, where thou dwellest, there will we abide until the end
opt3: Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life
opt4: We have forsaken all to build thy tabernacle in Galilee
correct: Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life
explanation: Peter recognized that Christ alone possesses the words of eternal life. John 6:68 (KJV) - "Then Simon Peter answered him, Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life."

question: What sobering warning did Jesus speak to the twelve concerning one of their own number?
opt1: One of you shall deny me before the cock crow

opt3: One of you is not of the seed of Abraham
opt4: Have not I chosen you twelve, and one of you is a devil?
correct: Have not I chosen you twelve, and one of you is a devil?
explanation: Jesus disclosed that Judas Iscariot would betray Him. John 6:70 (KJV) - "Jesus answered them, Have not I chosen you twelve, and one of you is a devil?"

question: Which Jewish feast was at hand when Jesus' brethren urged him to go into Judaea to show his works openly?
opt1: The Jews' feast of tabernacles
opt2: The feast of the Passover
opt3: The feast of Pentecost
opt4: The feast of the dedication
correct: The Jews' feast of tabernacles
explanation: The events of John 7 unfolded surrounding the Feast of Tabernacles. John 7:2 (KJV) - "Now the Jews' feast of tabernacles was at hand."

question: What did Jesus answer his brethren who pressed him to go up openly to the feast in Judaea?
opt1: I will go up with twelve legions of angels
opt2: My time is not yet come: but your time is alway ready
opt3: The Sanhedrin hath set a watch upon the highway
opt4: No prophet may show himself before the sabbath day
correct: My time is not yet come: but your time is alway ready
explanation: Jesus operated on a divine timetable ordained by His Father. John 7:6 (KJV) - "Then Jesus said unto them, My time is not yet come: but your time is alway ready."

question: Why did the Jews marvel when Jesus went up into the temple about the midst of the feast and taught?
opt1: Because he spake in the tongues of foreign nations
opt2: Because fire descended from heaven upon his words
opt3: How knoweth this man letters, having never learned?
opt4: Because the priests bowed before his teaching
correct: How knoweth this man letters, having never learned?
explanation: They marveled at His profound rabbinic knowledge without formal rabbinical schooling. John 7:15 (KJV) - "And the Jews marvelled, saying, How knoweth this man letters, having never learned?"

question: How did Jesus say a person can know whether his doctrine is of God or whether he spoke of himself?
opt1: By studying the traditions of the ancient elders
opt2: By examining his lineage through the house of David
opt3: By demanding a sign from heaven before the priests
opt4: If any man will do his will, he shall know of the doctrine, whether it be of God, or whether I speak of myself
correct: If any man will do his will, he shall know of the doctrine, whether it be of God, or whether I speak of myself
explanation: Spiritual discernment is granted to those whose hearts are yielded to obey God's will. John 7:17 (KJV) - "If any man will do his will, he shall know of the doctrine, whether it be of God, or whether I speak of myself."

question: What standard of evaluation did Jesus command regarding judging his actions on the sabbath?
opt1: Judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous judgment
opt2: Judge all men according to the strict letter of the circumcision
opt3: Judge no man, but commit all causes unto the high priest
opt4: Judge according to the multitude of witnesses
correct: Judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous judgment
explanation: Jesus commanded righteous judgment based on spiritual truth rather than superficial appearances. John 7:24 (KJV) - "Judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous judgment."

question: On the last day, that great day of the feast of tabernacles, what proclamation did Jesus cry out to the multitude?
opt1: Offer your sacrifices upon the brazen altar before sundown
opt2: If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink
opt3: Prepare ye the way of the King of glory
opt4: Repent, for the temple of stones shall be cast down
correct: If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink
explanation: During the water-libation ceremony, Jesus offered Himself as the source of living water. John 7:37 (KJV) - "In the last day, that great day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried, saying, If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink."

question: What did Jesus say would flow out of the belly of him that believeth on him, as the scripture hath said?
opt1: Sweet wine from the hills of Ephraim
opt2: The oil of gladness above his fellows
opt3: Rivers of living water
opt4: Torches of fire to illuminate the nations
correct: Rivers of living water
explanation: Believers become conduits of the Holy Spirit, depicted as rivers of living water. John 7:38 (KJV) - "He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water."

question: To what did the apostle John explain that Jesus was referring when he spoke of rivers of living water?
opt1: The rain that should bless the harvest of Israel
opt2: The words of the Law written on tables of stone
opt3: The blood of the new testament shed at Calvary
opt4: (But this spake he of the Spirit, which they that believe on him should receive: for the Holy Ghost was not yet given; because that Jesus was not yet glorified.)
correct: (But this spake he of the Spirit, which they that believe on him should receive: for the Holy Ghost was not yet given; because that Jesus was not yet glorified.)
explanation: John explains that this prophesied the outpouring of the Holy Spirit following Christ's glorification. John 7:39 (KJV) - "(But this spake he of the Spirit, which they that believe on him should receive: for the Holy Ghost was not yet given; because that Jesus was not yet glorified.)"

question: What answer did the temple officers give when the chief priests and Pharisees asked why they had not brought Jesus arrested?
opt1: Never man spake like this man
opt2: We feared the multitude, lest they stone us
opt3: He vanished out of our sight into the mount
opt4: Roman soldiers guarded his company
correct: Never man spake like this man
explanation: The arresting officers were utterly awestruck by Christ's divine authority and speech. John 7:46 (KJV) - "The officers answered, Never man spake like this man."

question: What legal principle of procedural justice did Nicodemus pose to the Pharisees when they condemned Jesus unheard?
opt1: No man may be condemned without three high priests consenting
opt2: Doth our law judge any man, before it hear him, and know what he doeth?
opt3: A Galilean prophet cannot be judged on the feast day
opt4: The Sanhedrin hath no power to condemn without Roman consent
correct: Doth our law judge any man, before it hear him, and know what he doeth?
explanation: Nicodemus reminded his colleagues of the Law's requirement of a fair, impartial hearing. John 7:51 (KJV) - "Doth our law judge any man, before it hear him, and know what he doeth?"

question: What answer did Jesus give to the scribes and Pharisees when they brought a woman taken in adultery and asked what should be done?
opt1: Stone her according to the strict commandment of Moses

opt3: He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her
opt4: The civil judgment belongeth unto the Roman governor
correct: He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her
explanation: Jesus convicted their hypocritical consciences by demanding sinlessness from her accusers. John 8:7 (KJV) - "So when they continued asking him, he lifted up himself, and said unto them, He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her."

question: What words of pardon and admonition did Jesus speak to the woman after her accusers departed one by one?
opt1: Offer two turtle doves at the altar for thy cleansing
opt2: Return to thy husband and fast forty days
opt3: Thy secret sins are covered by the mercy seat
opt4: Neither do I condemn thee: go, and sin no more
correct: Neither do I condemn thee: go, and sin no more
explanation: Jesus extended divine mercy while commanding her to forsake sin. John 8:11 (KJV) - "She said, No man, Lord. And Jesus said unto her, Neither do I condemn thee: go, and sin no more."

question: What supreme 'I AM' declaration did Jesus speak unto the people in the treasury of the temple?
opt1: I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life

opt3: I am the morning star that shineth upon the tribes of Jacob
opt4: I am the Lord of the sabbath and builder of the temple
correct: I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life
explanation: Jesus declared Himself the universal illumination dispelling moral darkness. John 8:12 (KJV) - "Then spake Jesus again unto them, saying, I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life."

question: What liberating promise did Jesus make to those Jews who believed on him if they continued in his word?
opt1: Ye shall possess the gates of your enemies in peace

opt3: Ye shall be delivered from the burden of Roman taxation
opt4: Ye shall rule over twelve cities in the kingdom of God

explanation: Spiritual liberation comes through experiential knowledge of divine truth. John 8:32 (KJV) - "And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free."

question: What definition of spiritual bondage did Jesus give when the Jews claimed they were never in bondage to any man?
opt1: He that payeth tribute to Caesar is a slave to the Gentiles

opt4: He that is uncircumcised is alienated from the commonwealth of Israel
correct: Whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin
explanation: Habitual sin enslaves the human soul to spiritual bondage. John 8:34 (KJV) - "Jesus answered them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin."

question: Whom did Jesus declare was the true spiritual father of those who sought to kill him and refused the truth?
opt1: Pharaoh king of Egypt

explanation: Jesus unmasked their murderous opposition as stemming directly from Satan. John 8:44 (KJV) - "Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him."

question: What piercing challenge of sinlessness did Jesus place before his theological adversaries?
opt1: Which of you convinceth me of sin? And if I say the truth, why do ye not believe me?

opt4: Have I taken silver or gold from any man in Israel?
correct: Which of you convinceth me of sin? And if I say the truth, why do ye not believe me?
explanation: Jesus boldly asserted His absolute moral perfection and impeccability. John 8:46 (KJV) - "Which of you convinceth me of sin? And if I say the truth, why do ye not believe me?"

question: What did Jesus say regarding Abraham's prophetic vision of Christ's advent?

opt4: Abraham saw my glory only in the smoke of Mount Sinai
correct: Your father Abraham rejoiced to see my day: and he saw it, and was glad
explanation: Abraham foresaw the Messianic day with joyful faith. John 8:56 (KJV) - "Your father Abraham rejoiced to see my day: and he saw it, and was glad."

question: What absolute claim to eternal self-existence did Jesus make, causing the Jews to take up stones to cast at him?

correct: Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am
explanation: Jesus used the divine covenant name 'I AM' (Exodus 3:14), declaring His eternal deity. John 8:58 (KJV) - "Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am."

question: What did Jesus do when the Jews took up stones to stone him after he claimed eternal deity?
opt1: He called down fire to consume their stones

question: What reason did Jesus give for why the man was born blind, refuting the disciples' assumption of parental or personal sin?
opt1: Neither hath this man sinned, nor his parents: but that the works of God should be made manifest in him

opt4: Because his mother failed to offer the purification sacrifice
correct: Neither hath this man sinned, nor his parents: but that the works of God should be made manifest in him
explanation: The man's blindness was permitted so God's redemptive power could be displayed. John 9:3 (KJV) - "Jesus answered, Neither hath this man sinned, nor his parents: but that the works of God should be made manifest in him."

question: What physical actions did Jesus perform before sending the blind man to wash in the pool of Siloam?

opt4: He took dust from the sanctuary and mingled it with water of the laver
correct: He spat on the ground, and made clay of the spittle, and he anointed the eyes of the blind man with the clay
explanation: Jesus applied clay made of spittle to the blind man's eyes. John 9:6 (KJV) - "When he had thus spoken, he spat on the ground, and made clay of the spittle, and he anointed the eyes of the blind man with the clay,"

question: What does the name of the pool 'Siloam' mean by interpretation, according to John?

opt3: Sent
opt4: Cleansing

explanation: John interprets Siloam as 'Sent', pointing to Christ the Sent One. John 9:7 (KJV) - "And said unto him, Go, wash in the pool of Siloam, (which is by interpretation, Sent.) He went his way therefore, and washed, and came seeing."

question: Why did the parents of the healed blind man fear to answer the Jews openly concerning who opened his eyes?

correct: Because the Jews had agreed already, that if any man did confess that he was Christ, he should be put out of the synagogue
explanation: The religious authorities had decreed excommunication for anyone confessing Christ. John 9:22 (KJV) - "These words spake his parents, because they feared the Jews: for the Jews had agreed already, that if any man did confess that he was Christ, he should be put out of the synagogue."

question: What unshakeable personal testimony did the healed man give when the Pharisees insisted that Jesus was a sinner?
opt1: Whether he be a sinner or no, I know not: one thing I know, that, whereas I was blind, now I see

opt4: Search your own scriptures and see if a sinner can give sight
correct: Whether he be a sinner or no, I know not: one thing I know, that, whereas I was blind, now I see
explanation: His indisputable experiential testimony silenced theological quibbles. John 9:25 (KJV) - "He answered and said, Whether he be a sinner or no, I know not: one thing I know, that, whereas I was blind, now I see."

question: What sound theological deduction did the healed man present to the council regarding Jesus' origin?
opt1: No prophet ariseth out of Galilee
opt2: If this man were not of God, he could do nothing
opt3: Moses spake with God, but this man speaketh with angels
opt4: He hath learned letters from the scribes of Babylon

explanation: The beggar argued logically that such a miracle requires divine power. John 9:33 (KJV) - "If this man were not of God, he could do nothing."

question: What did Jesus ask the healed man when he heard that the Pharisees had cast him out of the synagogue?
opt1: Wilt thou return unto thy parents in peace?

opt3: Dost thou believe on the Son of God?
opt4: Hast thou offered thy gift at the altar of Moses?
correct: Dost thou believe on the Son of God?
explanation: Jesus sought out the rejected man to lead him to saving faith. John 9:35 (KJV) - "Jesus heard that they had cast him out; and when he had found him, he said unto him, Dost thou believe on the Son of God?"

question: What was the healed man's response when Jesus identified Himself as the Son of God talking with him?
opt1: Lord, show me the Father, and it sufficeth me
opt2: I will tell all Jerusalem of thy majesty
opt3: Rabbi, thou art a prophet mighty in deeds
opt4: And he said, Lord, I believe. And he worshipped him
correct: And he said, Lord, I believe. And he worshipped him
explanation: The healed man confessed faith and rendered divine worship to Jesus. John 9:38 (KJV) - "And he said, Lord, I believe. And he worshipped him."

question: What judicial purpose for his coming into this world did Jesus enunciate in John 9?
opt1: For judgment I am come into this world, that they which see not might see; and that they which see might be made blind
opt2: To establish an earthly kingdom and abolish the Roman senate

opt4: To condemn the Gentiles and restore the twelve tribes of Israel
correct: For judgment I am come into this world, that they which see not might see; and that they which see might be made blind
explanation: Christ's ministry reveals spiritual blindness while granting sight to the humble. John 9:39 (KJV) - "And Jesus said, For judgment I am come into this world, that they which see not might see; and that they which see might be made blind."

question: What did Jesus reply when the Pharisees asked, 'Are we blind also?'
opt1: Ye are blind guides leading the blind into the ditch
opt2: If ye were blind, ye should have no sin: but now ye say, We see; therefore your sin remaineth
opt3: Thy blindness shall endure until the year of jubilee
opt4: Search the prophets, for your eyes have rejected their light
correct: If ye were blind, ye should have no sin: but now ye say, We see; therefore your sin remaineth
explanation: Their self-righteous claim to sight confirmed their culpable guilt. John 9:41 (KJV) - "Jesus said unto them, If ye were blind, ye should have no sin: but now ye say, We see; therefore your sin remaineth."

question: In the Parable of the Sheepfold, how does Jesus describe anyone who enters not by the door into the sheepfold, but climbs up some other way?
opt1: An hireling who careth not for the sheep
