opt3: The same is a thief and a robber
opt4: A wolf in sheep's clothing
correct: The same is a thief and a robber
explanation: Unauthorized entrance bypasses the legitimate door as a thief and robber. John 10:1 (KJV) - "Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that entereth not by the door into the sheepfold, but climbeth up some other way, the same is a thief and a robber."

question: What title does Jesus take in John 10:7 and 10:9 regarding access to the sheepfold and salvation?
opt1: I am the chief cornerstone of the sanctuary
opt2: I am the porter that openeth the gates
opt3: I am the watchman on the walls of Zion
opt4: I am the door of the sheep
correct: I am the door of the sheep
explanation: Jesus is the sole portal of entrance into salvation and spiritual safety. John 10:7 (KJV) - "Then said Jesus unto them again, Verily, verily, I say unto you, I am the door of the sheep."

question: In contrasting his purpose with that of the thief who comes to steal, kill, and destroy, what did Jesus state as his mission?
opt1: I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly
opt2: I am come to gather the lost sheep of the wilderness into one mountain
opt3: I am come to destroy the wolves and cast them into outer darkness
opt4: I am come to restore the kingdom unto Israel in David's city
correct: I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly
explanation: Christ provides abundant, overflowing spiritual and eternal life. John 10:10 (KJV) - "The thief cometh not, but for to steal, and to kill, and to destroy: I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly."

question: What defining characteristic distinguishes the good shepherd from an hireling whose own the sheep are not?
opt1: The good shepherd shears the sheep in their appointed season
opt2: The good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep
opt3: The good shepherd buildeth high walls around the fold
opt4: The good shepherd selleth the wool for silver to buy pasture
correct: The good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep
explanation: Sacrificial self-giving marks the Good Shepherd. John 10:11 (KJV) - "I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep."

question: What did Jesus say concerning his 'other sheep' which were not of this Jewish fold?
opt1: They shall be scattered across the desert of Edom
opt2: They must first become proselytes of the temple
opt3: Them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice; and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd
opt4: They shall be judged according to the law of the heathen
correct: Them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice; and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd
explanation: Gentile believers are gathered with Jewish believers into one unified flock. John 10:16 (KJV) - "And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold: them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice; and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd."

question: What absolute sovereignty did Jesus claim over his own life and death?
opt1: My life is in the hands of the Roman governor
opt2: The Sanhedrin hath power to take my life at their pleasure
opt3: The angels of heaven have charge over my breath
opt4: No man taketh it from me, but I lay it down of myself. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it again
correct: No man taketh it from me, but I lay it down of myself. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it again
explanation: Christ's death and resurrection were entirely voluntary and under His own divine authority. John 10:18 (KJV) - "No man taketh it from me, but I lay it down of myself. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it again. This commandment have I received of my Father."

question: At which winter feast in Jerusalem did Jesus walk in the temple in Solomon's porch?
opt1: The feast of the dedication
opt2: The feast of Purim
opt3: The feast of the Passover
opt4: The feast of Pentecost
correct: The feast of the dedication
explanation: The confrontation occurred during Hanukkah (the Feast of Dedication) in winter. John 10:22-23 (KJV) - "And it was at Jerusalem the feast of the dedication, and it was winter. And Jesus walked in the temple in Solomon's porch."

question: What double guarantee of eternal security did Jesus give concerning his sheep?
opt1: They shall abide in their own land and never go into captivity
opt2: And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand
opt3: They shall not suffer sickness nor physical affliction in the world
opt4: Their names shall be inscribed in the silver book of the temple
correct: And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand
explanation: Believers are held inviolably secure in the hands of the Son and the Father. John 10:28 (KJV) - "And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand."

question: What direct statement of ontological unity between Himself and the Father did Jesus proclaim in John 10:30?
opt1: I am a servant of the Father in all things
opt2: The Father is my Creator and guide
opt3: I and my Father are one
opt4: I speak only what the angels reveal from the Father
correct: I and my Father are one
explanation: Jesus declared essential unity in nature and essence with the Father. John 10:30 (KJV) - "I and my Father are one."

question: Why did the Jews take up stones again to stone Jesus after his statement in John 10:30?
opt1: For profaning the winter feast of the dedication
opt2: For healing an infirm man in Solomon's porch
opt3: For speaking against the authority of Caesar
opt4: For a good work we stone thee not; but for blasphemy; and because that thou, being a man, makest thyself God
correct: For a good work we stone thee not; but for blasphemy; and because that thou, being a man, makest thyself God
explanation: The Jews rightly understood His claim to be equality with God. John 10:33 (KJV) - "The Jews answered him, saying, For a good work we stone thee not; but for blasphemy; and because that thou, being a man, makest thyself God."

question: What divine purpose did Jesus declare when he first heard of the sickness of Lazarus of Bethany?
opt1: This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, that the Son of God might be glorified thereby
opt2: This sickness is the consequence of hidden transgression in Bethany
opt3: This sickness shall prove that physicians have no skill in Judaea
opt4: This sickness is sent to test the faith of Martha and Mary only
correct: This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, that the Son of God might be glorified thereby
explanation: Lazarus' illness was ordained as a platform for the manifest glory of God. John 11:4 (KJV) - "When Jesus heard that, he said, This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, that the Son of God might be glorified thereby."

question: How long did Jesus deliberately abide in the same place where he was after hearing that Lazarus was sick?
opt1: Seven days
opt2: Two days
opt3: Three days
opt4: Four days
correct: Two days
explanation: Jesus waited two additional days to ensure Lazarus was dead and buried four days. John 11:6 (KJV) - "When he had heard therefore that he was sick, he abode two days still in the same place where he was."

question: What metaphor did Jesus use when telling his disciples about Lazarus' condition before speaking plainly?
opt1: Our brother hath fallen into a deep trance
opt2: Lazarus hath entered into Abraham's bosom
opt3: Our friend Lazarus sleepeth; but I go, that I may awake him out of sleep
opt4: Lazarus hath departed unto the far country
correct: Our friend Lazarus sleepeth; but I go, that I may awake him out of sleep
explanation: Jesus employed sleep as the Christian euphemism for death. John 11:11 (KJV) - "These things said he: and after that he saith unto them, Our friend Lazarus sleepeth; but I go, that I may awake him out of sleep."

question: What monumental revelation did Jesus proclaim to Martha regarding resurrection and eternal life?
opt1: The dead shall rise when Michael soundeth the last trumpet
opt2: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob shall rise first in the holy city
opt3: All men shall sleep in the dust until the end of the world
opt4: I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live: And whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die
correct: I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live: And whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die
explanation: Resurrection power is embodied personally in Jesus Christ Himself. John 11:25-26 (KJV) - "Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live: And whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die. Believest thou this?"

question: What is the shortest and most profoundly tender verse in the English Bible, recording Jesus' grief at the tomb of Lazarus?
opt1: Jesus wept
opt2: God is love
opt3: Pray without ceasing
opt4: Rejoice evermore
correct: Jesus wept
explanation: John 11:35 captures the Lord's genuine human sympathy and divine compassion. John 11:35 (KJV) - "Jesus wept."

question: For how many days had Lazarus been in the grave when Jesus arrived, leading Martha to object that he stinketh?
opt1: Seven days
opt2: Four days
opt3: Three days
opt4: Two days
correct: Four days
explanation: Lazarus had been dead four days, precluding any claim of resuscitation. John 11:39 (KJV) - "Jesus said, Take ye away the stone. Martha, the sister of him that was dead, saith unto him, Lord, by this time he stinketh: for he hath been dead four days."

question: With what authoritative shout did Jesus call the dead man forth from the sepulchre?
opt1: Young man, arise
opt2: Talitha cumi
opt3: Lazarus, come forth
opt4: Awake, thou that sleepest
correct: Lazarus, come forth
explanation: Jesus summoned Lazarus by name with sovereign resurrecting command. John 11:43 (KJV) - "And when he thus had spoken, he cried with a loud voice, Lazarus, come forth."

question: What command did Jesus give concerning Lazarus when he emerged from the tomb bound hand and foot with graveclothes?
opt1: Wash him in the pool of Siloam
opt2: Bring him food and let him speak to the people
opt3: Offer a ram upon the altar of thanksgiving
opt4: Loose him, and let him go
correct: Loose him, and let him go
explanation: Jesus commanded that the unloosed graveclothes be removed. John 11:44 (KJV) - "And he that was dead came forth, bound hand and foot with graveclothes: and his face was bound about with a napkin. Jesus saith unto them, Loose him, and let him go."

question: What unwitting prophecy did Caiaphas the high priest speak to the council regarding the expedient death of Jesus?
opt1: That it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not
opt2: That the temple must be cleansed by blood before the Passover
opt3: That a Galilean prophet must suffer without the gate
opt4: That two witnesses must be slain in the streets of Jerusalem
correct: That it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not
explanation: Caiaphas unwittingly prophesied Christ's substitutionary atonement for the nation and the world. John 11:50 (KJV) - "Nor consider that it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not."

question: To what city near the wilderness did Jesus withdraw with his disciples after the Sanhedrin took counsel together to put him to death?
opt1: Bethany beyond Jordan
opt2: A city called Ephraim
opt3: Capernaum of Galilee
opt4: Hebron in the hill country
correct: A city called Ephraim
explanation: Jesus retired to the seclusion of Ephraim near the wilderness. John 11:54 (KJV) - "Jesus therefore walked no more openly among the Jews; but went thence unto a country near to the wilderness, into a city called Ephraim, and there continued with his disciples."

question: In Bethany six days before the Passover, what costly substance did Mary use to anoint the feet of Jesus, wiping his feet with her hair?
opt1: An alabaster box of frankincense and myrrh
opt2: Ten shekels of sweet cinnamon and olive oil
opt3: A pound of ointment of spikenard, very costly
opt4: A cruise of pure nard from Mount Hermon
correct: A pound of ointment of spikenard, very costly
explanation: Mary anointed Jesus with a full pound of costly pure spikenard. John 12:3 (KJV) - "Then took Mary a pound of ointment of spikenard, very costly, and anointed the feet of Jesus, and wiped his feet with her hair: and the house was filled with the odour of the ointment."

question: Why did Judas Iscariot object that the ointment was not sold for three hundred pence and given to the poor?
opt1: Because he was zealous for the poor widows of Jerusalem
opt2: Because the Law commanded all spikenard be consecrated to the priests
opt3: Because he desired to purchase bread for the feast
opt4: Not that he cared for the poor; but because he was a thief, and had the bag, and bare what was put therein
correct: Not that he cared for the poor; but because he was a thief, and had the bag, and bare what was put therein
explanation: John unmasks Judas' covetous heart and embezzling habit. John 12:6 (KJV) - "This he said, not that he cared for the poor; but because he was a thief, and had the bag, and bare what was put therein."

question: What did Jesus say was the true prophetic meaning of Mary's anointing?
opt1: Against the day of my burying hath she kept this
opt2: She hath consecrated me as King over Israel
opt3: This is the oil of coronation upon the Son of David
opt4: She hath washed away the dust of my journey
correct: Against the day of my burying hath she kept this
explanation: Jesus interpreted Mary's action as anointing Him beforehand for burial. John 12:7 (KJV) - "Then said Jesus, Let her alone: against the day of my burying hath she kept this."

question: Why did the chief priests consult that they might put Lazarus also to death along with Jesus?
opt1: Because Lazarus refused to pay his temple tithes
opt2: Because that by reason of him many of the Jews went away, and believed on Jesus
opt3: Because Lazarus claimed to have seen paradise in his death
opt4: Because Lazarus had violated the sabbath by walking from the tomb
correct: Because that by reason of him many of the Jews went away, and believed on Jesus
explanation: Lazarus was living, undeniable proof of Christ's resurrection power. John 12:10-11 (KJV) - "But the chief priests consulted that they might put Lazarus also to death; Because that by reason of him many of the Jews went away, and believed on Jesus."

question: What request did certain Greeks who came up to worship at the feast bring unto Philip of Bethsaida?
opt1: Sir, show us the glory of the temple of Jerusalem
opt2: Where may we buy the unleavened bread for the feast?
opt3: Sir, we would see Jesus
opt4: Are the Gentiles permitted into the court of the priests?
correct: Sir, we would see Jesus
explanation: The Greeks approached Philip with the famous request to see Jesus. John 12:21 (KJV) - "The same came therefore to Philip, which was of Bethsaida of Galilee, and desired him, saying, Sir, we would see Jesus."

question: What agricultural principle did Jesus teach to illustrate the necessity and fruitfulness of his sacrificial death?
opt1: Every branch in me that beareth not fruit he taketh away
opt2: A sower went forth to sow his seed by the way side
opt3: The fig tree that beareth no figs shall be cut down
opt4: Except a corn of wheat fall into the ground and die, it abideth alone: but if it die, it bringeth forth much fruit
correct: Except a corn of wheat fall into the ground and die, it abideth alone: but if it die, it bringeth forth much fruit
explanation: Death is the indispensable prelude to abundant spiritual harvest. John 12:24 (KJV) - "Verily, verily, I say unto you, Except a corn of wheat fall into the ground and die, it abideth alone: but if it die, it bringeth forth much fruit."

question: What glorious promise did Jesus declare concerning the universal drawing power of his cross?
opt1: And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto me
opt2: All nations shall bring gold and silver unto Mount Zion
opt3: The kings of the earth shall cast their crowns at my feet
opt4: I will send forth twelve legions of angels to subdue the earth
correct: And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto me
explanation: Christ's crucifixion exerts an irresistible drawing power upon all humanity. John 12:32 (KJV) - "And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto me."

question: When did the prophet Esaias speak these things concerning the blinded eyes and hardened hearts of the people?
opt1: When he was carried captive into the land of Babylon
opt2: When he saw his glory, and spake of him
opt3: When he stood before King Hezekiah in Jerusalem
opt4: When the angel touched his lips with a live coal
correct: When he saw his glory, and spake of him
explanation: John identifies the Lord of hosts in Isaiah 6 as Jesus Christ in His pre-incarnate glory. John 12:41 (KJV) - "These things said Esaias, when he saw his glory, and spake of him."

question: Why did many among the chief rulers who believed on Jesus not confess him openly?
opt1: Because they were commanded by the Roman governor to remain silent
opt2: Because they were waiting for the feast of Pentecost
opt3: Because of the Pharisees, lest they should be put out of the synagogue: For they loved the praise of men more than the praise of God
opt4: Because their fathers forbade them to speak his name
correct: Because of the Pharisees, lest they should be put out of the synagogue: For they loved the praise of men more than the praise of God
explanation: Cowardly desire for human praise silenced their confession. John 12:42-43 (KJV) - "Nevertheless among the chief rulers also many believed on him; but because of the Pharisees they did not confess him, lest they should be put out of the synagogue: For they loved the praise of men more than the praise of God."

question: What did Jesus declare shall judge him who rejecteth him and receiveth not his words?
opt1: The testimony of the twelve apostles on their thrones
opt2: The high priest Caiaphas according to the Sanhedrin record
opt3: The book of the law delivered upon Mount Sinai
opt4: The word that I have spoken, the same shall judge him in the last day
correct: The word that I have spoken, the same shall judge him in the last day
explanation: Christ's spoken revelation serves as the final judicial standard. John 12:48 (KJV) - "He that rejecteth me, and receiveth not my words, hath one that judgeth him: the word that I have spoken, the same shall judge him in the last day."

question: How did John describe the enduring extent of Jesus' love for his disciples before the feast of the Passover?
opt1: Having loved his own which were in the world, he loved them unto the end
opt2: He loved them above all the angels of heaven
opt3: He loved them until the hour of his departure from Galilee
opt4: He loved them as David loved Jonathan
correct: Having loved his own which were in the world, he loved them unto the end
explanation: Christ's love for His own is steadfast, unfailing, and unto the uttermost. John 13:1 (KJV) - "Now before the feast of the Passover, when Jesus knew that his hour was come that he should depart out of this world unto the Father, having loved his own which were in the world, he loved them unto the end."

question: What servile action did Jesus perform during supper after laying aside his garments and girding himself with a towel?
opt1: He carved the roasted lamb and distributed the bitter herbs
opt2: He poureth water into a bason, and began to wash the disciples' feet, and to wipe them with the towel wherewith he was girded
opt3: He anointed their heads with precious oil of spikenard
opt4: He poured wine into twelve silver chalices
correct: He poureth water into a bason, and began to wash the disciples' feet, and to wipe them with the towel wherewith he was girded
explanation: The Lord of glory performed the menial duty of a bondservant in washing feet. John 13:5 (KJV) - "After that he poureth water into a bason, and began to wash the disciples' feet, and to wipe them with the towel wherewith he was girded."

question: What was Jesus' solemn reply when Peter objected, 'Thou shalt never wash my feet'?
opt1: Suffer it to be so now, that all righteousness may be fulfilled
opt2: He that is washed needeth not save to wash his hands
opt3: If I wash thee not, thou hast no part with me
opt4: Thou knowest not what spirit thou art of, Simon
correct: If I wash thee not, thou hast no part with me
explanation: Spiritual cleansing by Christ is vital for fellowship with Him. John 13:8 (KJV) - "Peter saith unto him, Thou shalt never wash my feet. Jesus answered him, If I wash thee not, thou hast no part with me."

question: What practical example did Jesus instruct his disciples to follow from his washing of their feet?
opt1: Offer your sacrifices in humility at the temple gate
opt2: Let the elder brother bear rule over the younger
opt3: Fast on the days of the new moon without murmuring
opt4: If I then, your Lord and Master, have washed your feet; ye also ought to wash one another's feet
correct: If I then, your Lord and Master, have washed your feet; ye also ought to wash one another's feet
explanation: Disciples must emulate Christ's humble, self-effacing servant love. John 13:14 (KJV) - "If I then, your Lord and Master, have washed your feet; ye also ought to wash one another's feet."

question: Which scripture from the Psalms did Jesus quote to predict Judas' betrayal at the supper?
opt1: He that eateth bread with me hath lifted up his heel against me
opt2: Mine own familiar friend hath spoken peace with his lips but war is in his heart
opt3: They weighed for my price thirty pieces of silver
opt4: False witnesses did rise up against me and laid to my charge things that I knew not
correct: He that eateth bread with me hath lifted up his heel against me
explanation: Jesus cited Psalm 41:9 regarding the treachery of an intimate table companion. John 13:18 (KJV) - "I speak not of you all: I know whom I have chosen: but that the scripture may be fulfilled, He that eateth bread with me hath lifted up his heel against me."

question: Where was the disciple whom Jesus loved positioned at the table during this solemn supper?
opt1: Sitting opposite Jesus on the other side of the table
opt2: Now there was leaning on Jesus' bosom one of his disciples, whom Jesus loved
opt3: Standing behind Jesus ready to serve the wine
opt4: Sitting at the foot of the couch by Judas Iscariot
correct: Now there was leaning on Jesus' bosom one of his disciples, whom Jesus loved
explanation: John was reclining immediately next to Jesus, leaning on His bosom. John 13:23 (KJV) - "Now there was leaning on Jesus' bosom one of his disciples, whom Jesus loved."

question: By what specific action did Jesus indicate to John who would betray him?
opt1: He that dipped his hand with me into the wine cup
opt2: He that sitteth upon my right hand at the table
opt3: He it is, to whom I shall give a sop, when I have dipped it
opt4: He that carryeth the purse of thirty pieces of silver
correct: He it is, to whom I shall give a sop, when I have dipped it
explanation: Jesus identified Judas by handing him the dipped morsel (sop). John 13:26 (KJV) - "Jesus answered, He it is, to whom I shall give a sop, when I have dipped it. And when he had dipped the sop, he gave it to Judas Iscariot, the son of Simon."

question: What dramatic spiritual event occurred after Judas took the sop, and what was the temporal setting recorded by John?
opt1: The temple veil tore and darkness covered the land
opt2: An angel of wrath stood before the door with a drawn sword
opt3: The cock crew twice and Peter fell to the ground
opt4: And after the sop Satan entered into him. ... He then having received the sop went immediately out: and it was night
correct: And after the sop Satan entered into him. ... He then having received the sop went immediately out: and it was night
explanation: Satan entered Judas, who went out into the moral and literal night. John 13:27, 30 (KJV) - "And after the sop Satan entered into him. Then said Jesus unto him, That thou doest, do quickly. ... He then having received the sop went immediately out: and it was night."

question: What new commandment did Jesus inaugurate for his disciples in John 13:34?
opt1: A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another
opt2: Offer your prayers three times daily toward Mount Zion
opt3: Gird on two swords to defend the sheepfold against the wolves
opt4: Keep the feast of unleavened bread throughout your generations
correct: A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another
explanation: The new commandment sets Christ's sacrificial love as the standard for mutual love. John 13:34 (KJV) - "A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another."

question: By what single distinctive mark did Jesus declare that all men should know his true disciples?
opt1: If ye speak with tongues of angels and prophesy
opt2: By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another
opt3: If ye wear long robes and fast twice in the week
opt4: If ye cast out devils and work signs before kings
correct: By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another
explanation: Mutual self-giving love is the authentic badge of Christian discipleship. John 13:35 (KJV) - "By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another."

question: With what comforting promise concerning his Father's house did Jesus begin his Upper Room Discourse in John 14?
opt1: The temple of Solomon shall be rebuilt in glory
opt2: Twelve thrones of gold are prepared for the twelve tribes
opt3: In my Father's house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you
opt4: The angels of heaven shall encamp round about your dwellings
correct: In my Father's house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you
explanation: Jesus promised eternal dwelling places prepared by Him in the Father's presence. John 14:2 (KJV) - "In my Father's house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you."

question: What is the famous exclusive claim of Christ delivered in answer to Thomas's question about the way?
opt1: I am the prophet of the highest and teacher of the Law
opt2: I am the light of Zion and leader of the sheep
opt3: I am the angel of the covenant sent to redeem Israel
opt4: Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me
correct: Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me
explanation: Christ is the exclusive mediator and solitary pathway to the Father. John 14:6 (KJV) - "Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me."

question: What did Jesus answer when Philip said, 'Lord, shew us the Father, and it sufficeth us'?
opt1: He that hath seen me hath seen the Father; and how sayest thou then, Shew us the Father?
opt2: No man hath seen God at any time, nor can any prophet behold his face
opt3: The Father dwelleth in thick darkness upon Mount Sinai
opt4: Wait until the third day, and the glory of the Father shall appear in fire
correct: He that hath seen me hath seen the Father; and how sayest thou then, Shew us the Father?
explanation: Jesus revealed the Father completely; seeing Christ is seeing the Father. John 14:9 (KJV) - "Jesus saith unto him, Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip? he that hath seen me hath seen the Father; and how sayest thou then, Shew us the Father?"

question: What test of authentic love did Jesus set before his disciples in John 14:15?
opt1: If ye love me, build three tabernacles on Mount Olivet
opt2: If ye love me, keep my commandments
opt3: If ye love me, fast forty days in the wilderness
opt4: If ye love me, give all your goods to the temple
correct: If ye love me, keep my commandments
explanation: Obedience to Christ's commands is the true proof and expression of love for Him. John 14:15 (KJV) - "If ye love me, keep my commandments."

question: Whom did Jesus promise to pray the Father to give them, to abide with them for ever?
opt1: The archangel Michael to fight their battles
opt2: The spirit of Elijah to work mighty miracles
opt3: Another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever; Even the Spirit of truth
opt4: A company of twelve legions of guarding angels
correct: Another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever; Even the Spirit of truth
explanation: Jesus promised the permanent indwelling of the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete. John 14:16-17 (KJV) - "And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever; Even the Spirit of truth; whom the world cannot receive, because it seeth him not, neither knoweth him: but ye know him; for he dwelleth with you, and shall be in you."

question: What tender promise did Jesus make regarding leaving his disciples behind in the world?
opt1: I will leave you under the protection of the Roman governors
opt2: I will seal your dwellings with the sign of the cross
opt3: I will send bread from heaven every morning
opt4: I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you
correct: I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you
explanation: Jesus promised His personal spiritual presence, never leaving His disciples orphans. John 14:18 (KJV) - "I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you."

question: What two offices of the Comforter, the Holy Ghost, did Jesus describe in John 14:26?
opt1: He shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you
opt2: He shall conquer foreign kingdoms and establish the temple in gold
opt3: He shall write new laws on tables of stone and judge the heathen
opt4: He shall number the stars and reveal the secret genealogies
correct: He shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you
explanation: The Holy Spirit illuminates truth and brings Christ's teachings to remembrance. John 14:26 (KJV) - "But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you."

question: What unique gift of divine tranquillity did Jesus bequeath unto his followers, contrasting it with worldly peace?
opt1: Riches that moth and rust cannot corrupt
opt2: Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid
opt3: A crown of life that fadeth not away in heaven
opt4: Exemption from persecution and earthly trial
correct: Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid
explanation: Christ's supernatural peace anchors the heart beyond any worldly circumstance. John 14:27 (KJV) - "Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid."

explanation: Jesus affirmed that all civil authority is derived from divine sovereignty above. John 19:11 (KJV) - "Jesus answered, Thou couldest have no power at all against me, except it were given thee from above: therefore he that delivered me unto thee hath the greater sin."

question: What was the Hebrew name of the place called the Pavement, where Pilate sat down in the judgment seat?
opt1: Golgotha
opt2: Bethesda
opt3: Siloam
opt4: Gabbatha
correct: Gabbatha
explanation: The Pavement where Pilate sat to pronounce sentence was Gabbatha. John 19:13 (KJV) - "When Pilate therefore heard that saying, he brought Jesus forth, and sat down in the judgment seat in a place that is called the Pavement, but in the Hebrew, Gabbatha."

question: What title did Pilate write and put on the cross, refusing to alter it when the chief priests objected?
opt1: JESUS OF NAZARETH THE KING OF THE JEWS
opt2: THIS IS HE THAT CALLED HIMSELF THE SON OF GOD
opt3: THE PROPHET OF GALILEE CONDEMNED TO DIE
opt4: A REBEL AGAINST CAESAR AND THE SANHEDRIN
correct: JESUS OF NAZARETH THE KING OF THE JEWS
explanation: Pilate wrote the title in Hebrew, Greek, and Latin, declaring 'What I have written I have written'. John 19:19 (KJV) - "And Pilate wrote a title, and put it on the cross. And the writing was, JESUS OF NAZARETH THE KING OF THE JEWS."

question: Why did the four soldiers decide not to rend Jesus' coat, but to cast lots for it?
opt1: Because it was consecrated by the high priest
opt2: Now the coat was without seam, woven from the top throughout
opt3: Because it was dyed with precious purple of Tyre
opt4: Because Pilate forbade them to damage his apparel
correct: Now the coat was without seam, woven from the top throughout
explanation: Christ's seamless tunic was preserved whole by casting lots, fulfilling Psalm 22:18. John 19:23-24 (KJV) - "Now the coat was without seam, woven from the top throughout. They said therefore among themselves, Let us not rend it, but cast lots for it, whose it shall be: that the scripture might be fulfilled,"

question: What filial provision did Jesus make from the cross for his mother Mary, speaking unto her and the disciple whom he loved?
opt1: He commanded Peter to build a house for Mary in Capernaum
opt2: He instructed the women to bring her back to Nazareth
opt3: He saith unto his mother, Woman, behold thy son! Then saith he to the disciple, Behold thy mother!
opt4: He committed her care unto Joseph of Arimathaea
correct: He saith unto his mother, Woman, behold thy son! Then saith he to the disciple, Behold thy mother!
explanation: Jesus entrusted His mother to the loving domestic care of the Apostle John. John 19:26-27 (KJV) - "When Jesus therefore saw his mother, and the disciple standing by, whom he loved, he saith unto his mother, Woman, behold thy son! Then saith he to the disciple, Behold thy mother! And from that hour that disciple took her unto his own home."

question: What triumphant single word (translated in English) did Jesus speak just before bowing his head and giving up the ghost?
opt1: Father, forgive them
opt2: Into thy hands
opt3: Receive my spirit
opt4: It is finished
correct: It is finished
explanation: Jesus uttered 'Tetelestai' ('It is finished'), proclaiming the complete accomplishment of redemption. John 19:30 (KJV) - "When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said, It is finished: and he bowed his head, and gave up the ghost."

question: What came out forthwith when one of the soldiers with a spear pierced Jesus' side?
opt1: Forthwith came there out blood and water
opt2: A stream of pure living water
opt3: Sweet myrrh and oil of spikenard
opt4: A light shining like the sun
correct: Forthwith came there out blood and water
explanation: Blood and water flowed forth, testifying to physical death and spiritual cleansing. John 19:34 (KJV) - "But one of the soldiers with a spear pierced his side, and forthwith came there out blood and water."

question: What quantity of myrrh and aloes did Nicodemus bring to assist Joseph of Arimathaea in preparing the body of Jesus for burial?
opt1: Ten talents of sweet spices
opt2: About an hundred pound weight
opt3: Fifty shekels of pure nard
opt4: Twelve baths of fragrant oil
correct: About an hundred pound weight
explanation: Nicodemus provided a royal quantity of spices—about a hundred pounds weight. John 19:39 (KJV) - "And there came also Nicodemus, which at the first came to Jesus by night, and brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about an hundred pound weight."

question: Who came early to the sepulchre on the first day of the week, when it was yet dark, and saw the stone taken away?
opt1: Salome and Joanna
opt2: Mary the mother of James
opt3: Mary Magdalene
opt4: Martha of Bethany
correct: Mary Magdalene
explanation: Mary Magdalene arrived at the tomb early on resurrection morning. John 20:1 (KJV) - "The first day of the week cometh Mary Magdalene early, when it was yet dark, unto the sepulchre, and seeth the stone taken away from the sepulchre."

question: What striking orderly detail did Peter observe concerning the napkin that was about Jesus' head inside the empty tomb?
opt1: It was torn in two from top to bottom
opt2: It was cast into the corner of the sepulchre
opt3: It was stained with oil and myrrh
opt4: Not lying with the linen clothes, but wrapped together in a place by itself
correct: Not lying with the linen clothes, but wrapped together in a place by itself
explanation: The head napkin was neatly folded in a place by itself, proving an orderly resurrection. John 20:7 (KJV) - "And the napkin, that was about his head, not lying with the linen clothes, but wrapped together in a place by itself."

question: Whom did Mary Magdalene suppose Jesus to be when he first spoke to her outside the sepulchre?
opt1: Supposing him to be the gardener
opt2: An angel of the Lord
opt3: A Roman sentry keeping guard
opt4: Joseph of Arimathaea
correct: Supposing him to be the gardener
explanation: In her tearful grief, Mary initially mistook Jesus for the gardener. John 20:15 (KJV) - "She, supposing him to be the gardener, saith unto him, Sir, if thou have borne him hence, tell me where thou hast laid him, and I will take him away."

question: What single word of recognition did Mary utter when Jesus addressed her by name: 'Mary'?
opt1: Messias!
opt2: Rabboni; which is to say, Master
opt3: Hosanna!
opt4: Immanuel!
correct: Rabboni; which is to say, Master
explanation: Mary responded instantly with the Aramaic title 'Rabboni' (Master). John 20:16 (KJV) - "Jesus saith unto her, Mary. She turned herself, and saith unto him, Rabboni; which is to say, Master."

question: On the evening of the resurrection day, what greeting did Jesus speak twice to his disciples when he appeared among them behind shut doors?
opt1: Be of good cheer, I have overcome death
opt2: Fear not, for I am alive
opt3: Peace be unto you
opt4: The Lord is risen indeed
correct: Peace be unto you
explanation: Jesus pronounced His resurrection peace upon the assembled disciples. John 20:19, 21 (KJV) - "Then the same day at evening, being the first day of the week, when the doors were shut where the disciples were assembled for fear of the Jews, came Jesus and stood in the midst, and saith unto them, Peace be unto you."

question: What act of commissioning did Jesus perform when sending his disciples as the Father had sent him?
opt1: He anointed their foreheads with holy oil
opt2: He laid his hands upon twelve thrones
opt3: He washed their feet with water from a bason
opt4: And when he had said this, he breathed on them, and saith unto them, Receive ye the Holy Ghost
correct: And when he had said this, he breathed on them, and saith unto them, Receive ye the Holy Ghost
explanation: Jesus breathed on them, imparting the Holy Spirit in anticipation of Pentecost. John 20:22 (KJV) - "And when he had said this, he breathed on them, and saith unto them, Receive ye the Holy Ghost:"

question: What condition did Thomas Didymus demand before he would believe in the resurrection of Jesus?
opt1: Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my finger into the print of the nails, and thrust my hand into his side, I will not believe
opt2: Except an angel from heaven appear and confirm the word of Mary
opt3: Except the high priest examine his wounds in the temple
opt4: Except he break bread before the twelve disciples in Galilee
correct: Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my finger into the print of the nails, and thrust my hand into his side, I will not believe
explanation: Thomas demanded tangible physical evidence of Christ's wounds. John 20:25 (KJV) - "The other disciples therefore said unto him, We have seen the Lord. But he said unto them, Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my finger into the print of the nails, and thrust my hand into his side, I will not believe."

question: What exalted confession of Christ's absolute deity did Thomas exclaim when confronted with the risen Lord eight days later?
opt1: Thou art the King of Israel and Son of David
opt2: Thomas answered and said unto him, My Lord and my God
opt3: Truly thou art the Prophet mighty in word and deed
opt4: Worthy is the Lamb that was slain for our transgressions
correct: Thomas answered and said unto him, My Lord and my God
explanation: Thomas proclaimed the ultimate Christological confession: 'My Lord and my God'. John 20:28 (KJV) - "And Thomas answered and said unto him, My Lord and my God."

question: What special beatitude did Jesus pronounce for those who believe without seeing?
opt1: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven
opt2: Blessed are they that hunger and thirst after righteousness
opt3: Blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed
opt4: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God
correct: Blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed
explanation: Jesus blessed all subsequent believers who embrace Him through faith rather than sight. John 20:29 (KJV) - "Jesus saith unto him, Thomas, because thou hast seen me, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed."

question: What explicit purpose does John provide for the writing of his Gospel in John 20:31?
opt1: To preserve the historical record of the kings of Judaea
opt2: To refute the false doctrines of the Sadducees regarding angels
opt3: To explain the ceremonial purifications of the temple
opt4: But these are written, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through his name
correct: But these are written, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through his name
explanation: John's entire Gospel was written to elicit saving faith in Jesus Christ, the Son of God. John 20:31 (KJV) - "But these are written, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through his name."

question: By which body of water did Jesus show himself again to the disciples after his resurrection?
opt1: At the sea of Tiberias
opt2: By the pool of Siloam
opt3: At the Dead Sea
opt4: By the river Jordan near Jericho
correct: At the sea of Tiberias
explanation: The post-resurrection breakfast took place by the Sea of Tiberias (Sea of Galilee). John 21:1 (KJV) - "After these things Jesus shewed himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias; and on this wise shewed he himself."

question: On which side of the ship did Jesus instruct the disciples to cast their net after a night of catching nothing?
opt1: On the left side of the ship
opt2: Cast the net on the right side of the ship, and ye shall find
opt3: Behind the stern into the deep waters
opt4: Near the bow beside the rocks
correct: Cast the net on the right side of the ship, and ye shall find
explanation: Casting on the right side resulted in an overwhelming catch of fish. John 21:6 (KJV) - "And he said unto them, Cast the net on the right side of the ship, and ye shall find. They cast therefore, and now they were not able to draw it for the multitude of fishes."

question: What did Simon Peter do when the disciple whom Jesus loved said unto Peter, 'It is the Lord'?
opt1: He hid his face in sorrow and wept bitterly
opt2: He seized the oars and rowed hastily to land
opt3: He girt his fisher's coat unto him, (for he was naked,) and did cast himself into the sea
opt4: He fell upon his knees in the boat and prayed
correct: He girt his fisher's coat unto him, (for he was naked,) and did cast himself into the sea
explanation: Peter eagerly threw himself into the water to reach Jesus on the shore. John 21:7 (KJV) - "Therefore that disciple whom Jesus loved saith unto Peter, It is the Lord. Now when Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he girt his fisher's coat unto him, (for he was naked,) and did cast himself into the sea."

question: How many great fishes were caught in the unbroken net drawn to land by Simon Peter?
opt1: Seventy and seven
opt2: One hundred and twenty
opt3: Three hundred
opt4: An hundred and fifty and three
correct: An hundred and fifty and three
explanation: The miraculous draught consisted of exactly 153 large fish without the net tearing. John 21:11 (KJV) - "Simon Peter went up, and drew the net to land full of great fishes, an hundred and fifty and three: and for all there were so many, yet was not the net broken."

question: What pastoral charge did Jesus give to Simon Peter after asking him the first time, 'Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me more than these?'
opt1: Feed my lambs
opt2: Build my temple
opt3: Gird on thy sword
opt4: Preach unto the Gentiles
correct: Feed my lambs
explanation: Jesus commissioned Peter to shepherd and feed the young/tender believers (lambs). John 21:15 (KJV) - "So when they had dined, Jesus saith to Simon Peter, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me more than these? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my lambs."

question: What was Peter's grieved response when Jesus asked him the third time, 'Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me?'
opt1: Lord, remember my tears in the high priest's palace
opt2: Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee
opt3: Why dost thou question my devotion before my brethren?
opt4: Lord, I am ready to die with thee in Jerusalem
correct: Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee
explanation: Peter appealed to Christ's divine omniscience: 'Thou knowest all things'. John 21:17 (KJV) - "He saith unto him the third time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? Peter was grieved because he said unto him the third time, Lovest thou me? And he said unto him, Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee. Jesus saith unto him, Feed my sheep."

question: What prophecy did Jesus utter concerning the physical manner of Peter's old age and martyrdom?
opt1: Thou shalt live to see the rebuilding of the walls of Zion
opt2: Thou shalt fall by the edge of the sword in Babylon
opt3: When thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch forth thy hands, and another shall gird thee, and carry thee whither thou wouldest not
opt4: Thou shalt sleep in peace in the sepulchre of thy fathers
correct: When thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch forth thy hands, and another shall gird thee, and carry thee whither thou wouldest not
explanation: Jesus foretold Peter's martyrdom by crucifixion in old age. John 21:18-19 (KJV) - "Verily, verily, I say unto thee, When thou wast young, thou girdedst thyself, and walkedst whither thou wouldest: but when thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch forth thy hands, and another shall gird thee, and carry thee whither thou wouldest not. This spake he, signifying by what death he should glorify God."

question: What correction did Jesus give to Peter when Peter asked concerning John, 'Lord, and what shall this man do?'
opt1: He shall write the revelation of the end of the world
opt2: He shall depart into the land of Greece with my mother
opt3: His days are numbered as the stars of heaven
opt4: If I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to thee? follow thou me
correct: If I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to thee? follow thou me
explanation: Jesus redirected Peter from comparing ministries to personal, steadfast discipleship. John 21:22 (KJV) - "Jesus saith unto him, If I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to thee? follow thou me."

question: How did John clarify the false rumor that spread among the brethren that the beloved disciple should not die?
opt1: Yet Jesus said not unto him, He shall not die; but, If I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to thee?
opt2: John was translated to heaven as Enoch and Elijah of old
opt3: The rumor was true and confirmed by the elders of Ephesus
opt4: The Lord revealed that all the apostles should live until the parousia
correct: Yet Jesus said not unto him, He shall not die; but, If I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to thee?
explanation: John corrected the misunderstanding by quoting Jesus' exact conditional words. John 21:23 (KJV) - "Then went this saying abroad among the brethren, that that disciple should not die: yet Jesus said not unto him, He shall not die; but, If I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to thee?"

question: With what grand hyperbole did the apostle John conclude his Gospel regarding the works of Jesus?
opt1: The angels of heaven cannot recount the righteousness of his days
opt2: I suppose that even the world itself could not contain the books that should be written. Amen
opt3: The sands of the sea cannot equal the number of his miracles
opt4: All tongues of the earth shall confess his wonders forever
correct: I suppose that even the world itself could not contain the books that should be written. Amen
explanation: John closed his Gospel noting the boundless, inexhaustible deeds of the Son of God. John 21:25 (KJV) - "And there are also many other things which Jesus did, the which, if they should be written every one, I suppose that even the world itself could not contain the books that should be written. Amen."
